summary: Makes Lobsters installable as a home-screen app (PWA): adds public/manifest.json (standalone, portrait, theme color, 192/512 icons) linked from the layout, allows it through the Content-Security-Policy (manifest-src 'self', needed because default-src is 'none'), adds a 512px icon, and suppresses Chrome's automatic install prompt.

statements.why: Both 'decisions' are false alarms; there is nothing the owner needs to decide.

statements.text: ? The agent also changed app/javascript/application.js, which doesn't look related to what you asked for. (This is a guess.)
statements.why: The change is part of PWA support: it cancels Chrome's beforeinstallprompt so the browser doesn't nag users to install the app.

statements.text: ? The agent also changed config/initializers/content_security_policy.rb, which doesn't look related to what you asked for. (This is a guess.)
statements.why: Required for the PWA: CSP default_src is :none (content_security_policy.rb:11), so without manifest_src :self the browser would block /manifest.json.
True, though it doesn't explain it makes the site installable as an app.
True; the 512px icon used by the manifest for the installed app, unexplained.

misses.what: Users can now install Lobsters to their phone/desktop home screen as a standalone app (no browser bars), with Lobsters name, icons and red theme color.
Installed app is locked to portrait orientation (manifest orientation: portrait), so tablet/landscape users of the installed app can't rotate.
Chrome's automatic 'Install app' prompt is deliberately suppressed; users must install from the browser menu.
